note: Words drawn twice within one coordinate bucket collapse to one printed token.
Words within three vertical points form one printed line.
Numeric starts within twelve horizontal points form one candidate column.
A printed value joins its nearest column only within twenty-five coordinate points.
The row-label band ends eight points before the first value centre.
Two function words classify a candidate header line as prose.
A vertical gap exceeding two and one-half row pitches starts a new table block.
A vertical gap also exceeds the row pitch by eight points before starting a new block.
At least four non-space characters are required before duplicate-draw repair.
A column with fewer members is a stray mark.
The dense core locates the band; populated nearby leading columns and every column to the right stay, while a distant vintage embedded before a fund name stays in the row label.
The dense core requires at least three values.
The dense core retains columns carrying at least forty percent of the page peak.
A gap wider than this multiple of the typical gap may separate label digits from values.
Only one or two clusters before a wide gap may be discarded as label material.
A legitimate sparse leading value column may sit up to two typical column gaps left of the dense core.
A sparse leading extension remains within sixty-five coordinate points of the dense core.
A leading extension must carry at least twenty percent of the page peak and at least the dense-core floor.
An overlapping draw interleaves the words; ignoring whitespace the sequence is a literal repeat.
A phrase first uses the nearest column hint; an unhinted phrase uses its strongest value-span overlap, which prevents one label from contaminating neighbouring columns.
Two qualifying printed header lines combine from top to bottom.
At most two consecutive header rows govern one table.
Words within one column phrase may be separated by seven points.
Adjacent single-character text-layer fragments rejoin without inserted spaces.
A small number or footnote marker immediately after a phrase stays with that phrase.
An unhinted phrase needs two points of overlap with a value span.
A phrase more than twenty-five points from a column centre remains unassigned.
A table header search stops one hundred twenty points above its first row.
A first header candidate must sit within forty vertical points of the table; this excludes a continuation page title.
A header candidate must land in at least two distinct columns.
A text header candidate must name at least two columns.
A year-only statement header must name at least two columns.
A detached numeric unit joins only within three and one-half horizontal points on the same line.
A one-row block is removed only when it is prose, a header, or contains two numeric tokens assigned to one cell.
Only the physically adjacent prior page may supply continuation headers.
Continuation columns must remain within fifteen coordinate points.
The donor page must immediately precede the receiving page.
A complete leading year column folds only when every printed row label is a period label or contains no alphabetic name.
At least three populated years establish a year column.
Later blocks on the same page inherit the last qualifying header.
The page summary uses the row header set with the most named columns instead of whichever block appeared first.
